mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 2.5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to persistent higher real borrowing costs compressing equity discounting.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a zero-move baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS drops below 2.5% within the next 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in hourly wage growth (indirect via UNRATE) predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as weak labor demand outweighs any short-term inflation relief.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% month-over-month and UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In 60-day windows where such triggers occur, the 20-day forward returns are positive or at least not statistically different from baseline (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in retail sales (HOUST) exceeding 2% for three consecutive months is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it signals resilient consumer demand and upward earnings revisions.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >2% each month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 12 such months, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a zero-move baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month coincides with a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as it reflects weakening manufacturing momentum and downward earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% in a single month
failure_condition: During such events, the 20-day forward returns are not negative or at least not statistically significant (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to market anticipation of aggressive rate hikes that erode equity valuations.
failure_condition: In such regimes, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly different from a zero-move baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.5% and a rise in labor force participation (implied via complement proxies not available here) is expected to drive a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as it signals full employment momentum.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% and remains below for the next month
failure_condition: Over 10 such episodes, the 20-day forward returns are not positive or not statistically significant (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in consumer confidence proxies (not directly available; using HOUST as a demand proxy) of 4% or more for two months predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as it indicates deteriorating sentiment and spending restraint.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by >4% each month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During such pullbacks, the 60-day forward returns are not negative or at least not significantly worse than baseline (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer confidence proxy (HOUST) move in opposite directions—INDPRO falls while HOUST rises by more than 2% in the same month—the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive, reflecting offsetting supply and demand pressures.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >2% and HOUST increases by >2% in the same month
failure_condition: In 20-day windows with such cross-pressures, the forward returns are not positive or not statistically significant (p > 0.1).
